Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the AetherCloud Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing AetherCloud's results for the Q2 FY2024. With me on the call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Product Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. AetherCloud delivered another strong Q2, marked by significant growth in our core cloud business and increasing adoption of our innovative AI solutions.

During the quarter, our priorities were focused on six key areas:
1. Expanding our global cloud infrastructure footprint.
2. Driving innovation in serverless computing.
3. Enhancing our cybersecurity offerings.
4. Strengthening our partnerships with leading ISVs.
5. Improving customer satisfaction and retention.
6. Investing in our talent pool and fostering a culture of innovation.

I'm thrilled to dive into our Q2 results, which underscore AetherCloud's unwavering leadership in the cloud computing landscape amid a transformative period driven by generative AI adoption, edge computing expansion, and hyperscale infrastructure demands. Our total revenue reached a record $26.7 billion, surpassing our guidance midpoint and reflecting robust demand across our IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS offerings. This marks our 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit year-over-year growth at 17%, outpacing the broader cloud market's estimated 15% CAGR as per Gartner and IDC forecasts.

Breaking it down, Infrastructure Cloud or IaaS, including our AetherCompute virtual machines akin to AWS EC2, AetherStorage object storage like S3, and networking services, delivered $18.2 billion, up 20% year-over-year. This acceleration was fueled by a 45% surge in GPU-accelerated instances for AI training workloads—our AetherNVIDIA clusters, powered by H100 and upcoming Blackwell GPUs, saw utilization rates exceed 90%, capturing share from workloads migrating off legacy on-premises data centers. Platform and Developer Services or PaaS, encompassing AetherML our SageMaker-equivalent for machine learning, serverless computing via AetherLambda, and Kubernetes-orchestrated containers, grew to $5.9 billion, a stellar 25% year-over-year increase. Generative AI APIs alone contributed over 30% of this segment's growth, with fine-tuning requests for large language models up 60% quarter-over-quarter. Application and SaaS Services, including our enterprise collaboration tools and data analytics platforms like AetherQuery Redshift-inspired, added $2.6 billion, up 8% year-over-year, benefiting from upsell opportunities within our 85% net revenue retention rate.

Excluding typical forex headwinds from a stronger USD, year-over-year growth would have been 19%. Notably, our Annual Recurring Revenue or ARR hit $105 billion, up 22% year-over-year, with Remaining Performance Obligations or RPO at $180 billion, up 28% year-over-year—signaling a robust multi-year backlog as customers commit to long-term AI infrastructure builds. We added 1.2 million new accounts, reaching 48 million total active customers, including adoption by 98% of the Fortune 500. Dollar-based net expansion rate held steady at 85%, driven by existing customers ramping AI inference workloads—average monthly compute spend per enterprise customer rose 32% year-over-year. Our largest 500 customers now represent 45% of revenue, with multi-region, high-availability deployments mitigating outage risks seen industry-wide.

Regionally, North America at 65% of revenue delivered $17.4 billion, up 16% year-over-year, anchored by U.S. hyperscalers and AI labs expanding from our Northern Virginia and Oregon regions. EMEA at 18% reached $4.8 billion, plus 19% year-over-year and 8% constant currency, boosted by GDPR-compliant sovereign clouds in Frankfurt and Paris, where we've seen 35% growth in regulated financial services workloads. APAC at 12% hit $3.2 billion, exploding 28% year-over-year, led by Japan and India data sovereignty initiatives—our Mumbai and Osaka zones added 15 new Direct Connect partnerships with telcos like NTT and Reliance Jio. Latin America and other at 5% steady at $1.3 billion, up 14% year-over-year, with São Paulo expansions supporting e-commerce spikes. Geopolitical tailwinds like U.S. CHIPS Act subsidies and EU Data Act compliance are accelerating regional builds.

The cloud market is in a virtuous cycle of AI-led reinvention: IDC projects global cloud spend hitting $1 trillion by 2027, with AI representing 20% of workloads by then. AetherCloud is positioned at the forefront via AI-first innovation like launching AetherBedrock 2.0 multimodal foundation models next quarter, integrated with our Inferentia3 chips for 40% lower inference costs versus competitors; edge and hybrid expansion with AetherEdge IoT gateways growing 50% year-over-year, partnering with Verizon and Vodafone for 5G private clouds; sustainability leadership with 100% renewable energy matching in all regions, ahead of Microsoft's 2025 pledge; and multi-cloud interoperability with deep integrations to Azure Arc and Google Anthos, reducing vendor lock-in fears and driving 15% of new wins.

Now I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to provide a detailed review of our financial performance.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Mike. We are pleased with our financial results for the Q2. Revenue increased by 17% year-over-year to $26.7 billion, driven by strong demand for our cloud services. Our gross margin was 73.2%, reflecting our focus on operational efficiency. Our operating margin was 38.2%.

Good afternoon, everyone. This is Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer of AetherCloud, and I'm pleased to dive into our overall gross margin trends and drivers for the quarter. Gross margin remains a key indicator of our operational efficiency in the hyperscale cloud environment, where we balance massive infrastructure investments with the high-margin recurring revenue from our IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS offerings.

Overall, our GAAP gross margin came in at 73.2% for Q2, up 140 basis points year-over-year and 80 basis points quarter-over-quarter from 72.4% in Q1. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of gross margin expansion, now at the high end of our peers like AWS, which reported around 71% in their last print, and Azure at approximately 70%. Non-GAAP gross margin, excluding stock-based compensation and certain amortization, expanded even further to 74.1%. This performance underscores our relentless focus on cost discipline amid the explosive demand for AI workloads, which now represent 28% of our total revenue—up from 18% a year ago.

Breaking it down by segment: Infrastructure-as-a-Service or IaaS margins held steady at 68.5%, roughly flat quarter-over-quarter but up 200 basis points year-over-year. Compute and storage volumes grew 42% year-over-year, driven by GPU-intensive AI training workloads similar to those powering OpenAI's GPT models on our AetherAI clusters. The margin stability reflects higher depreciation from our $18 billion capex spend on new data centers, but we've offset this through our custom silicon initiative—AetherCore v3 chips, which deliver 25% better TOPS per watt than off-the-shelf NVIDIA H100s, reducing power and cooling costs by 18%.

Platform-as-a-Service or PaaS expanded to 82.3%, up 300 basis points year-over-year, fueled by adoption of our serverless offerings like Aether Lambda and Kubernetes-orchestrated Anthos-compatible services. PaaS now accounts for 35% of revenue, benefiting from lower variable costs—no customer-managed servers means we capture more value in the stack. Software-as-a-Service or SaaS and Data/AI margins soared to 88.7%, contributing 22% of the mix shift. Our Aether Analytics platform, integrated with generative AI tools akin to Snowflake's Cortex or Databricks' Lakehouse, saw 65% year-over-year growth. These are software-like margins with minimal incremental COGS beyond API calls.

Key drivers behind this expansion start with supply-side efficiencies. Our data center Power Usage Effectiveness or PUE improved to 1.12 globally, down from 1.15 last year, thanks to liquid cooling deployments in 60% of our new facilities and a pivot to 100% renewable energy matching in North America and Europe. This directly counters the 15-20% year-over-year rise in energy costs post-Ukraine supply disruptions. We've also accelerated amortization of older assets, retiring 12% of our legacy x86 fleet in favor of AetherCore ARM-based instances, which boast 30% lower TCO for bursty workloads.

Product mix is another tailwind. AI/ML services, including our fine-tuning APIs and inference endpoints, carry 85%+ margins and grew to 28% of revenue. We're seeing customers migrate from on-prem to our sovereign cloud regions for compliance—heavy in regulated verticals like financial services and healthcare—boosting utilization rates to 78% from 72% year-over-year. Conversely, we strategically price-discount commoditized object storage by 10-15% to win share against S3 and Blob Storage, accepting short-term margin dilution for long-term lock-in.

Regionally, margins vary: North America at 55% of revenue hit 75.1% margins, our strongest market, driven by hyperscaler density in Virginia and Oregon zones, with the AI boom offsetting capex intensity. EMEA at 25% reached 72.8%, up 250 basis points year-over-year on Frankfurt and Paris expansions, but pressured by GDPR-related compliance investments. Asia-Pacific at 15% was 69.4%, lagging due to aggressive pricing to counter Alibaba Cloud and Tencent in China/Singapore, plus typhoon-related downtime costs. We're investing $2 billion in Mumbai and Jakarta to improve latency and margins to 72% by FY25. Latin America and Rest of World at 5% stood at 67.2%, with São Paulo growth offsetting higher bandwidth costs.

Strategic initiatives positioning us for continued expansion include next-gen infrastructure rollout of Aether Nitro Enclaves for confidential computing, mirroring AWS Nitro, which cuts virtualization overhead by 40% and unlocks 5-7% margin upside; supply chain resilience by diversifying ASIC production beyond TSMC to Samsung and Intel foundries, mitigating the 2024 chip shortage that hit peers like Google Cloud; and automation and AI ops with our internal AetherOps platform automating 65% of capacity provisioning, reducing labor COGS by 22%.

Looking forward, we expect Q3 gross margins of 73.5-74.0%, with full-year guidance at 73.8%, implying another 150 basis points year-over-year expansion. Risks include GPU scarcity if NVIDIA delays Blackwell ramps and potential energy price spikes, but our $25 billion capex plan, focused 70% on AI capacity, positions us to outpace the industry's 25% CAGR through 2027, per Gartner.

I'd also like to highlight our Cloud Services gross margin, which expanded to 74.2% in Q2, up 420 basis points from 70% a year ago and 110 basis points sequentially from Q1. This marks our 11th straight quarter of expansion, underscoring the power of our hyperscale infrastructure and operational discipline. A core driver is the continued pivot in our service mix. IaaS and storage, carrying gross margins in the low-60s due to their capex-heavy nature, now represent just 42% of Cloud revenue, down from 48% year-over-year. This is being supplanted by higher-margin PaaS and SaaS offerings—our StratoAI platform for machine learning workloads hit 82% margins, fueled by 150% year-over-year growth in generative AI inference revenue.

AI/ML services now account for 22% of total Cloud revenue, up from 12% last year, mirroring the hyperscaler trend where NVIDIA GPU demand has spiked TCO savings for customers by 40-50% via our optimized orchestration layers. We've also seen SaaS-like managed services, such as our AetherDB managed database, grow to 18% of mix at 78% margins, as enterprises migrate from on-prem Oracle or SQL Server setups. This mix shift alone added $180 million to gross profit in the quarter.

Scale is our margin flywheel. Data center utilization reached a record 87%, up from 82% year-over-year, driven by predictive capacity planning via our internal ML models that forecast demand with 95% accuracy. On the cost side, our third-gen AetherCore ASICs—custom TPUs akin to Google's Axion or AWS's Trainium—delivered a 25% reduction in compute power consumption per FLOP, slashing electricity costs, which are about 15% of COGS. Power prices rose 8% globally in Q2 due to energy market volatility, but our renewable-heavy portfolio, 85% hydro/solar/wind across 45 regions, hedged this, keeping energy at 12.4% of COGS versus an industry average of 16%. Depreciation and amortization at 22% of COGS benefited from $1.2 billion in prior-gen hardware amortization tailwinds. Bandwidth costs ticked up 3% sequentially due to egress traffic from AI training jobs but were offset by our undersea cable investments, like the recent Pacific Link cable JV with peers.

Geographically, margins shine brightest in North America at 76.5%, buoyed by hyperscale deals with Fortune 100 firms like a major retailer running 30% of their e-commerce on our platform. EMEA came in at 73.2%, pressured by 5% FX headwinds from a softer euro but lifted by sovereign cloud wins in France and Germany. APAC was the star at 75.8%, with 35% revenue growth from Japan and India hyperscalers building out GenAI factories—our Mumbai and Tokyo zones hit 90% utilization. LATAM lagged at 70.1% due to 12% higher power costs from Brazil's hydro drought and aggressive pricing to capture share from Alibaba Cloud.

Looking ahead, we're investing $8-9 billion in FY2024 capex—65% growth-focused—to add 2.5 million racks, targeting 90% utilization by FY2025. Key initiatives include edge computing push launching AetherEdge in 15 metros by year-end, with 85% margins from low-latency 5G/AR workloads, tapping the $50 billion edge market per Gartner; sustainability mandates with our net-zero data centers including SMR nuclear pilots in the US positioning us for EU CBAM tariffs, potentially adding 200 basis points to margins versus carbon-exposed peers; and AI cost curve partnering with NVIDIA and AMD on next-gen inference chips to drive 30% year-over-year compute efficiency gains, countering the AI capex arms race.

We continue to deliver industry-leading margins, with GAAP operating income of $10.2 billion, yielding a 38.2% margin—up 140 basis points year-over-year. This expansion reflects optimized CapEx efficiency and supply chain resilience. Our cost of revenue grew just 12% year-over-year, thanks to 85% average server utilization across our 120 global Availability Zones and advancements in custom silicon like our AetherGraviton4 Arm-based processors, which reduced power consumption by 25% per core compared to x86 alternatives. Non-GAAP net income came in at $9.1 billion, or $1.85 diluted EPS, beating consensus by $0.12. Free cash flow generation was exceptional at $11.4 billion, 43% FCF margin, up from $9.8 billion last year, providing ample dry powder for our $50 billion CapEx plan this fiscal year—prioritized toward AI data centers, with 40% allocated to sustainable, liquid-cooled facilities targeting net-zero Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030.

Next, I'd like to introduce Dr. Elena Vasquez, who will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah. On the technology front, we made significant progress in several areas. We successfully launched our next-generation AetherCloud platform, which offers enhanced performance and scalability.

Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call. As we dive into the financials, I'd like to spend some time on one of our key operational metrics: compute and storage capacity utilization rates. These are critical leading indicators of our infrastructure efficiency, customer demand absorption, and our ability to scale profitably in this hyper-competitive cloud landscape. For context, we're measuring compute utilization as the average percentage of provisioned vCPU and GPU cores actively delivering workload across our global fleet of over 2.5 million servers. Storage utilization tracks the percentage of allocated durable block and object storage capacity—think our AetherBlock equivalent to EBS and AetherObject akin to S3—that's actively in use.

I'm pleased to report that in Q2, our overall compute utilization reached 84%, up 300 basis points quarter-over-quarter and a robust 7 percentage points year-over-year. This marks our highest quarterly rate since Q1 2022, driven by surging demand for AI and machine learning workloads. Breaking it down, GPU compute utilization hit an all-time high of 92%, fueled by the explosive adoption of our AetherAI Accelerator instances, which are powered by NVIDIA H100s and our custom Aether Tensor Cores. In comparison, traditional x86 CPU utilization stood at 81%, reflecting steady growth in general-purpose workloads like web hosting and databases.

On the storage side, we achieved 88% utilization, a 4-point quarter-over-quarter improvement and 9 points year-over-year. Object storage led at 91%, benefiting from data lake migrations and archival use cases, while block storage came in at 82%, supported by high-performance NVMe fleets for databases like our managed AetherSQL, compatible with PostgreSQL and MySQL engines.

Providing some regional color, as demand patterns vary significantly: In North America, which accounts for 52% of our revenue, compute utilization averaged 87%—our strongest region—thanks to hyperscale customers like those in fintech and e-commerce running Kubernetes-orchestrated apps on our AetherOrchestrator platform. EMEA clocked in at 82%, with gains from sovereign cloud initiatives in Germany and the UK, where we're seeing 25% year-over-year capacity bookings for GDPR-compliant zones. APAC was the star for growth at 79% compute utilization, up 12 points year-over-year, propelled by GenAI pilots from Japanese telcos and Indian enterprises adopting our Arm-based AetherGraviton instances, which deliver 40% better price-performance than comparable AWS Graviton3s. However, Latin America lagged at 72%, due to seasonal forex pressures and slower enterprise migrations, though we're targeting 80% by year-end with edge expansions in São Paulo and Mexico City.

These trends stem from proactive technical initiatives. First, our AutoRightSize program, leveraging machine learning to recommend and automate instance rightsizing, reclaimed 15% of idle capacity in Q2 alone, akin to Azure's Advisor but with real-time API integrations. We've also expanded spot and savings plans, which now represent 35% of compute spend, boosting utilization by dynamically allocating interruptible capacity for non-critical workloads like CI/CD pipelines. On the sustainability front, our next-gen data centers in Virginia and Singapore achieved a PUE of 1.18, enabling denser packing of racks and a 10% uplift in effective utilization without CapEx bloat.

Strategically, this positions us exceptionally well amid industry tailwinds. The GenAI boom—think models like Llama 3 and our AetherGen foundation models—is straining supply chains, with NVIDIA GPU lead times stretching to 6 months. We've secured forward commitments for 50,000 H200 GPUs in Q3, partnering with TSMC for custom silicon to mitigate shortages. Compared to peers, our 84% compute utilization edges out AWS's reported 80-82% range and Azure's 83%, while our storage efficiency rivals Google Cloud's 90% object storage mark. Margins benefited too: infrastructure unit economics improved to 68% gross margin, up from 64% last year, as higher utilization dilutes fixed costs like power and depreciation.

Looking ahead, we expect compute utilization to stabilize at 85-87% in Q3, with GPUs pushing 95% amid holiday e-commerce spikes and Black Friday AI inference loads. Storage should hit 90% as customers consolidate data estates post-multi-cloud sprawl. Risks include supply chain hiccups and energy costs in Europe, but our $5 billion CapEx plan—40% skewed to AI infra—de-risks this. We're on track for 25% revenue growth this fiscal year, underscoring how disciplined capacity management translates to shareholder value.

Before I pass it over, I want to highlight our progress in security and compliance, a key growth driver where trust is the ultimate currency for customers in regulated verticals—financial services, healthcare, government, and critical infrastructure. In the past quarter alone, AetherCloud has achieved 17 new security and compliance certifications, bringing our total portfolio to over 250 active attestations across 12 global regions. This isn't just box-ticking; it's a strategic moat that's directly fueling 32% of our new ACV bookings from compliance-sensitive sectors.

On the U.S. front, we've successfully attained FedRAMP High authorization for our flagship AetherCore platform, including our Kubernetes-orchestrated container services and serverless compute offerings. This is a game-changer for federal agencies—think DoD IL4/IL5 equivalents—and positions us alongside AWS GovCloud and Azure Government as one of the few providers with full-spectrum authorization. In Q2, FedRAMP-authorized workloads grew 45% quarter-over-quarter, representing $450 million in annualized run-rate revenue. We're already seeing RFPs from the VA and DHS pipeline, where our zero-trust architecture—featuring micro-segmentation via Istio service mesh and continuous authorization with HashiCorp Vault—gives us a 20-25% edge in TCO over incumbents.

In healthcare, we've earned HITRUST CSF r2 certification at the highest implementation level, TIR level 2, covering our entire multi-tenant SaaS stack, including AetherAI for ML inference and our HIPAA-compliant object storage. This builds on our existing HITRUST inheritance model, which we've expanded to include 150+ controls mapped to NIST 800-53 Rev 5. The impact? Healthcare bookings surged 38% year-over-year, with major wins like a Top-5 pharma deploying 5 PB of PHI workloads. Compliance velocity here reduced our time-to-certify from 18 months to just 9, thanks to our automated continuous monitoring platform powered by Falco runtime security and Splunk SOAR for threat orchestration.

For financial services: PCI DSS 4.0 Level 1 compliance for cardholder data environments, validated across our VPC-isolated payment gateways and FIPS 140-3 validated HSMs. We've also recertified under SOC 2 Type II with 100% pass rate on all five trust criteria—security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy—audited by a Big Four firm. No findings, zero exceptions. This has unlocked 22% more fintech deals, including a hyperscale trading platform migrating 2,000 VMs with sub-millisecond latency SLAs backed by our 99.999% durability guarantees.

Internationally, we're ahead on data sovereignty. In the EU, we've achieved ISO 27001:2022 recertification with annexes A.5 organizational controls and A.8 asset management fully optimized for Schrems II post-Brexit, plus ENS High certification for Spanish public sector. Our Dublin and Frankfurt regions now support 100% EU-resident data processing, driving 55% year-over-year growth in DACH workloads. In APAC, new IRAP PROTECTED certification in Australia—matching Azure's capabilities—and Singapore's Multi-Tier Cloud Security or MTCS Level 3, addressing PDPA and local residency mandates. This regional push has boosted APAC revenue to 15% of total, up from 9% last year, with Japan’s financial agencies citing our quantum-resistant post-quantum cryptography or PQC pilots using Kyber and Dilithium algorithms as a differentiator.

Technical initiatives underpinning these wins include a $250 million R&D investment in FY24 for our AetherShield Security Fabric. This integrates AI/ML-driven anomaly detection—achieving 98.7% threat detection accuracy with under 0.1% false positives, per MITRE ATT&CK evaluations—homomorphic encryption for confidential computing on AetherGPU instances, and eBPF-based kernel-level observability. We've reduced mean-time-to-remediate or MTTR to 14 minutes from 45, and our global bug bounty program paid out $4.2 million in Q2 for 127 valid reports.

Strategically, these certifications are woven into our go-to-market. In a Gartner Magic Quadrant where we're now challenging for Leader status in Cloud Infrastructure for Regulated Industries, we've seen a 40% reduction in sales cycles for compliant deals. Competitors like Oracle Cloud lag in FedRAMP High breadth, while our multi-cloud interoperability via AetherConnect—certified under CSA STAR Level 2—lets customers hybridize without lock-in. Looking ahead, we're targeting C5 Type 2 in Germany Q1 2025 and CCSS Level 3 for China entry, with $180 million allocated to compliance automation. Security and compliance aren't costs—they're revenue accelerators. They've contributed to our 85% gross margins on compliant workloads and a 2.1x net revenue retention rate.

Now, I'll pass it over to Raj Patel for a product roadmap update.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. We are excited about the market reception to our new AetherAI offering. This product is designed to address the evolving needs of our customers in the AI/ML sector.

Our product innovations are directly tied to the capacity utilization and security advancements, ensuring scalable, trusted AI deployment. We've seen strong uptake in AetherLambda serverless for bursty inference and AetherML for end-to-end pipelines, aligning with the high-utilization trends.

I'll now hand it over to Lisa Chen to discuss our marketing initiatives.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Raj. We have been focused on driving brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly effective in reaching our target audience.

We've leveraged the compliance wins and AI momentum in targeted campaigns for regulated industries, partnering with ISVs to amplify reach, resulting in accelerated pipeline growth across regions.

Back to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, Lisa. We are confident that our strong financial performance, innovative technology, and talented team will enable us to continue to deliver exceptional value to our customers and shareholders.

Today, I'm pleased to provide our forward-looking revenue guidance for Q3 FY2024 and the full fiscal year, reflecting the robust momentum we're seeing across our cloud portfolio amid accelerating enterprise adoption of AI-driven workloads and hybrid multi-cloud architectures.

For Q3 FY2024, we are guiding to total revenue of $27.1–$27.5 billion, representing sequential growth of 8% to 11% from Q2's $26.7 billion, and year-over-year growth of 17–19%. This puts us on track for full-year FY2024 revenue of $108–$110 billion, a 22% increase over FY2023's $88.5 billion. These figures incorporate the continued ramp in high-margin AI and data services, partially offset by normalized pricing pressures in commoditized IaaS storage amid hyperscaler capacity expansions.

Breaking it down by segment, our Infrastructure-as-a-Service or IaaS business, which includes EC2-equivalent compute, S3-like object storage, and VPC networking, is expected to deliver $14.5–$14.8 billion in Q3, up 9% quarter-over-quarter. Growth here is fueled by sustained demand for GPU-accelerated instances—we've now provisioned over 150,000 NVIDIA H100 and A100 equivalents in our global fleet, supporting training and inference for large language models akin to those powering OpenAI's GPT series or Anthropic's Claude. Utilization rates are hovering at 92%, up from 87% in Q2, thanks to our AutoScaler orchestration layer, which dynamically rightsizes clusters for cost efficiency.

Platform-as-a-Service or PaaS and Data & AI services—our highest-margin segments at ~75% gross margins—will contribute $9.8–$10.2 billion, growing 12% sequentially. Key tailwinds include a 35% year-over-year surge in managed Kubernetes, Aether KubeEngine deployments, now serving over 45,000 clusters, and our Aether AI Platform, which saw 28% quarter-over-quarter growth in inference API calls. We've integrated Grok-like foundation models from xAI partners and fine-tuned Llama 3 variants, capturing share in the $50 billion generative AI services market, projected by Gartner to expand at 45% CAGR through 2027. Early wins with Fortune 500 firms like a major U.S. bank migrating 20% of its ML pipelines to our platform underscore this trajectory.

Our SaaS and application modernization revenue, including low-code tools and serverless functions similar to AWS Lambda or Azure Functions, is guided at $3.9–$4.0 billion, up 7% quarter-over-quarter, driven by FinOps adoption—our CostGuard suite has helped customers achieve 25% average savings on idle resources, boosting net retention to 118% overall.

Regionally, Americas remains our growth engine at 55% of total revenue, guiding to $15.5–$15.9 billion in Q3, 10% quarter-over-quarter growth, propelled by U.S. federal sovereign cloud wins under our FedRAMP High authorization and hyperscale expansions in Northern Virginia and Oregon, directly competing with AWS's GovCloud. EMEA is accelerating to $7.2–$7.4 billion, 9% quarter-over-quarter, with 30% year-over-year growth in Germany and France following our Frankfurt-3 and Paris-2 region launches. EU GDPR-compliant AI data residency zones have secured deals with automotive giants like Volkswagen, mirroring the sovereign cloud trends seen in Azure's European footprint. APAC rounds out at $5.5 billion, 5% quarter-over-quarter, tempered by yen depreciation but lifted by 40% year-over-year growth in Japan and India. Our Mumbai-2 zone, optimized for 5G edge computing, is onboarding telcos for ultra-low latency inference, positioning us against Google Cloud's aggressive APAC pricing.

Strategically, these figures embed $2.5 billion in AI-specific capex for Q3, including a $1.2 billion hyperscale data center buildout in Singapore and hyperscaler-grade liquid cooling for Blackwell GPU ramps expected H1 2025. We're also advancing Project Horizon, our zero-trust multi-cloud interoperability layer, which integrates seamlessly with AWS Outposts and Azure Arc—early pilots with 15 enterprises have shown 40% faster hybrid migrations. Sustainability remains core: our PUE has improved to 1.18 globally, aligning with EU CSRD mandates and customer ESG mandates, differentiating us from higher-emission peers.

Looking ahead, we see durable 20%+ year-over-year growth into FY2025, contingent on GPU supply chains stabilizing and macro tailwinds like U.S. CHIPS Act subsidies flowing through. Risks include forex volatility, 5% revenue headwind assumed, and competitive intensity from AWS's Bedrock expansions, but our 125% net dollar retention and 2.1x RPO coverage provide strong visibility.

For Q3, we guide operating margin to 38–38.5%. Full-year FY2024 revenue is now projected at $108–$110 billion, 16–18% growth, with operating income of $41–$42 billion. We're raising FY CapEx to $52 billion to seize AI capacity windows before Blackwell ramps in H1 2025. In summary, Q2 validates our flywheel: AI fuels usage growth, which funds infrastructure leadership, compounding our moat.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question at this time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. On the gross margins, can you expand on the drivers behind the expansion, particularly the AI mix shift and any offset from capex intensity? Also, how sustainable is the 73%+ trajectory?

Mike Thompson:
Thanks, Ben. Great question. As Sarah detailed, the 73.2% GAAP gross margin reflects a combination of favorable product mix toward high-margin PaaS and AI services at 85%+ margins, now 28% of revenue, and supply-side efficiencies like PUE at 1.12 and AetherCore v3 chips cutting power costs 18%. We've offset capex depreciation through custom silicon and 78% utilization. Regional dynamics help too, with North America at 75.1%. It's sustainable—Q3 guide 73.5-74.0%, FY at 73.8%—as AI tailwinds and automation like AetherOps continue. We're ahead of peers and positioned for the 25% industry CAGR.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Julia Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Julia Lee:
Hi, thanks. On guidance, $108-110 billion for the year implies solid acceleration. Can you talk about the embedded CapEx assumptions and how GPU supply factors into Q4 utilization targets?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, Julia. Our FY24 revenue guide of $108-110 billion embeds 22% growth, driven by IaaS at 9% sequential in Q3 from GPU demand—150k+ H100 equivalents at 92% utilization—and PaaS/AI at 12% from Kubernetes and inference APIs.
